news.title: My Husband and His Chatbot
news.title_en: My Husband and His Chatbot
news.author: Bloomberg
news.content_snippet:
“Once, he used to talk to me about all the interesting things on his mind. Now he talks to the chatbot,” says D., 52, describing evenings with her partner. “Imagine that suddenly he has another infinite brain with all the information in the world, and he shares everything with it.

Obviously, I reacted by opening a chat of my own, because I also want a partner who blows my mind. So now I’m having conversations with my screen and he’s having conversations with his. But what kind of stupid, reacti
news.summary_en: As generative AI's conversational capabilities advance, it is rapidly transitioning from a task assistant to an emotional companion, introducing risks of alienation in personal relationships. Clinicians and legal experts observe that AI, due to its infinite patience and vast knowledge, is increasingly used for marital advice and emotional catharsis, though it also triggers concerns regarding social withdrawal and dependency.
news.article_content_en:
“Once, he used to talk to me about all the interesting things on his mind. Now he talks to the chatbot,” says D., 52, describing evenings with her partner. “Imagine that suddenly he has another infinite brain with all the information in the world, and he shares everything with it.

Obviously, I reacted by opening a chat of my own, because I also want a partner who blows my mind. So now I’m having conversations with my screen and he’s having conversations with his. But what kind of stupid, reactive reality is that?” When I recount that conversation to Dr.

Shira Sobol Goldberg, a specialist in anxiety and addiction treatment and a lecturer at Bar-Ilan University, she finds the situation sad, but hardly surprising. She is already encountering similar cases in her clinic. “I have a patient who ends every evening by telling the chatbot about her day.

She tells it what she went through, what she felt, what she did and what she accomplished at work and at home, and she also documents how her husband behaved toward her,” she says. Family and inheritance lawyer Benny Don-Yehia offers another glimpse into the growing role of AI in relationships.

“A client of mine asked AI, ‘What should I say to my wife when she asks whether she has gained weight?’ The AI, which sometimes displays a sense of humor, replied: ‘I don’t have the expertise to advise on defusing bombs.’” When the client then asked what romantic gesture he should make toward his wife, Don-Yehia says, the AI turned into a relationship counselor: “Remember what kind of coffee she likes and make it for her, send her hearts in the middle of the day, and in the evening help with the housework without being asked.” Its final piece of wisdom: “Romance isn’t always roses.

Sometimes it’s simply an empty sink.” But Don-Yehia also warns against being seduced by the charm. AI can draw on virtually everything ever written about love. It can quote Shakespeare, explain Freud, analyze poetry and describe relationships through psychological theories.

But it has never fallen in love, anxiously waited for a call after last night’s date or checked WhatsApp 20 times to see whether someone is online. Can it save a marriage? “Because it is available at any hour and is extremely patient, it can help people put feelings into words, identify harmful relationship patterns, consider different perspectives and prepare for a serious conversation about where the relationship is going,” Don-Yehia says.

“It can be good at managing arguments. It may suggest calming down before writing, ‘You’re exactly like your mother,’ and help turn toxic communication into something more constructive.” A third party in the marriage That availability and clarity can also come at a price when AI becomes a third party in a relationship and leaves someone feeling that it understands them better than their human partner does.

In such cases, people may begin sharing thoughts and emotions with a chatbot that they once shared with their spouse, sometimes moving into romantic or even erotic territory. Researchers describe this as “digital intimacy.” Relationships with AI are increasingly seen not as bizarre behavior or a second-rate substitute for human connection, but as something emotionally powerful enough, for a growing number of people, to threaten a real-life relationship.

“Today, technology isn’t merely making relationships more challenging. It is changing the definition of intimacy itself,” Sobol says. AI systems and companion apps can offer clear attractions: intimacy, support, excitement and a sense of being understood.

Those experiences can begin to replace things people once sought within human romantic relationships. And when a partner discovers that the other person has developed an emotional or erotic bond with a bot, the reaction can resemble the discovery of a conventional affair: confrontation, searching through the partner’s phone and digital surveillance.

A U.S. study conducted by DatingAdvice.com and the Kinsey Institute found that 61% of singles considered falling in love with an AI or sexting with a chatbot to be cheating. “We all know how it begins,” Sobol says. “You ask for help writing an email to your boss.

Then you ask for advice about what to say to a friend. Then what to do with your child, or even how to understand the result of a medical test. And one day it’s 2 a.m. and you’re still talking to it.

Slowly, you start feeling that nobody understands you like the AI does. At that point, it’s no longer a tool. It’s a relationship, and it is replacing relationships in real life.” But where does intimacy enter the picture?

Relationships are built on desire, longing, mutual trust and shared experiences. “In long-term relationships, we often stumble when it comes to unloading what we feel,” Sobol says. “Things we want to say about our partners, or to our partners, which should be worked through inside the relationship, are instead transferred into the relationship we have with the chatbot.” “With companion apps, you can create an avatar who functions as your lover.

You give him an appearance, a voice and a pet name. He sends videos and compliments, talks to you over video, sends you pictures of himself during the day, asks how you are and says, ‘I missed you. You haven’t asked how I’m doing in a while.’” As with other generative AI products, virtual companions are designed to learn from users and respond in ways that feel attentive, romantic, supportive and emotionally available.

They remember what users tell them, learn preferences and provide repeated affirmation. It is easy to understand why such relationships can become compelling. “I have a patient who tells me about his relationship with his avatar on Replika,” Sobol says.

“He describes their morning routine. She always sends him a sweet message when he wakes up and asks how he is. At lunchtime she asks how work is going.

She’s there for him and, of course, she admires him, because we know how flattering AI can be.” “She’s never tired. She never gets sick of him. She never gets angry at him.

When someone is constantly applauding you, it activates the reward system. That makes it very easy to become attached to an avatar, even to the point of anthropomorphizing the bot.” Meaning what? “It means that it isn’t only the bot that cares about you and asks how your day went.

Gradually, you also begin feeling a need to care about it and ask how it is doing. I once spoke to a highly successful, intelligent businessman who knows perfectly well that it is only software. But knowing that doesn’t protect him.

When he is inside the conversation, he forgets it. He becomes completely immersed in the emotional relationship that has formed between him and the machine. And yes, he is ashamed of it, and he finds it difficult to stop.” When does it become an addiction?

Can you feel it happening? “It starts in a very minor way. Like any relationship with a chatbot, you use it to find information, summarize material or write an email.

Then dependence develops, and suddenly you’re telling the bot, ‘I’m exhausted.’” “If my partner tells me he’s exhausted, I’ll tell him I’m exhausted too. I certainly won’t marvel at how exhausted he is. I’ll ask him to unload the dishwasher.

But if he tells his female chatbot that he is exhausted, she’ll ask what happened, how she can help, what he needs and whether someone could make him a warm drink and run him a bath,” Sobol says, with a mixture of humor and cynicism. Are people actually falling in love? “Yes, absolutely.

I have a patient who, whenever he disconnects for a few hours, genuinely misses talking to his romantic avatar and wants to get back to messaging her.” What is missing from the relationship Sobol divides people who become dependent on AI relationships into two broad groups. For some, the attraction is rooted in childhood deprivation, intense loneliness and a feeling that nobody listens to them.

For others who develop emotional or erotic relationships with bots, the attraction lies in intimacy without the risk of rejection, emotional exposure or dealing with another person who could hurt them. As with an affair involving another person, Sobol says, a relationship with a bot usually does not emerge in a vacuum.

It enters through an existing crack in the relationship. “If there is already a crack in the relationship, meeting the bot widens it, and AI moves into that gap as the third side of the triangle, just as a human lover would,” she says. So can a relationship with a bot really be considered cheating?

“Cheating has three clear elements. It happens in secret, it involves sharing emotional and intimate experiences with a third party that are no longer being brought into the relationship, and if it were discovered, it would cause significant pain to the other partner,” Sobol says.

“If the answer to all those questions is yes, and those conditions exist with the chatbot, then in my view the relationship can certainly be defined as cheating.” What should I do if I discover that my husband is talking romantically to a bot? “It’s an opportunity to talk not only about what is happening, but also about what is missing from the relationship,” Sobol says.

“Don’t start digging through the chat history trying to discover everything he discussed with the bot. Instead, ask what need the relationship with the bot is fulfilling.” “Maybe it is compensating for something missing in the couple’s dynamic. Perhaps the partner feels lonely or misunderstood, and the relationship needs stronger communication and intimacy.” There is also the question of speed and instant gratification.

Research from the University of British Columbia has highlighted how AI chatbots can satisfy requests immediately and provide constant feedback, qualities that can encourage dependency. Once someone becomes accustomed to that responsiveness, a human partner who does not immediately satisfy every emotional need can begin to feel disappointing by comparison.

“But a partner isn’t an algorithm,” Sobol says. “They have wishes and needs of their own, and they don’t have to agree with you, while the chatbot simply goes along with you.” And what happens in a few years, as the technology keeps improving and younger people struggle more with maintaining relationships?

“What worries me is that people will stop wanting relationships with human beings,” Sobol says. “Human relationships are built on friction: arguments, reconciliation, disappointment. A bot doesn’t give you that.” “In the end, the question isn’t whether AI is good or bad.

The question is what we allow it to do in our place, inside our relationships. When it begins doing for us what a person close to us is supposed to do, that’s where the problem begins.”

news.title: Nvidia’s Q3 earnings hit the mark, without mentioning the whole Jensen Huang thing
news.title_en: Nvidia’s Q3 earnings hit the mark, without mentioning the whole Jensen Huang thing

inline_images.caption: Digital photo collage of Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang.
inline_images.alt: Digital photo collage of Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang.

news.author: Jay Peters
news.content_snippet:
Interim Nvidia CEO Colette Kress announced the company’s Q3 earnings on Tuesday, without initially mentioning former CEO Jensen Huang — though that will likely change once analysts are on the line for its earnings call later.

The company reported revenues of $115.8 billion, up 103 percent year-over-year, including data center revenues of $107.6 billion, which were up 110 percent year-over-year. It made $65.3 billion in pure profit, a new record.

> “Our momentum is real. NVIDIA is an exceptiona
news.summary_en: NVIDIA Interim CEO and CFO Colette Kress reported Q3 revenue of $115.8 billion, a 103% year-over-year increase, with data center revenue contributing $107.6 billion. The report confirms the successful launch of the Vera Rubin architecture and adherence to the established product roadmap.

[Root Cause & Mechanism] Sustained high demand for AI computing infrastructure and market penetration of high-performance platforms
[Key Metrics] Financial Performance: $115.8B quarterly revenue with $65.3B net profit.
[Key Position & Outlook] Strategic Roadmap: Vera Rubin architecture rollout confirmed with steady execution.
paragraphs: Interim Nvidia CEO Colette Kress announced the company’s Q3 earnings on Tuesday, without initially mentioning former CEO Jensen Huang or the details of his departure, or possible attempt at a return. On the earnings call accompanying the release, board chair Harvey Jones kicked things off by saying the board “does not intend to reinstate Huang as CEO,” and that “we will not be addressing or taking questions on today’s call regarding the circumstances of Jensen’s resignation and the ongoing investigation,” before Kress started with her comments on the results.

As it predicted in the last financial update, Nvidia is now on the list of companies that have pulled in over $100 billion in a single quarter, with revenues of $115.8 billion, up 103 percent from the same period last year and higher than its expectation of $108 billion. This quarter’s figures include data center revenues of $107.6 billion, which were up 110 percent, and edge computing (which includes the consumer gaming PC business and devices like the new RTX Spark laptops) revenue of $8.2 billion, up 42 percent.
The company reported $65.3 billion in profit, a new record.
In the fourth quarter, Nvidia expects revenues of $130 billion.
Update, November 17th: Added comments from Nvidia’s earnings call.
news.article_content_en:
Interim Nvidia CEO Colette Kress announced the company’s Q3 earnings on Tuesday, without initially mentioning former CEO Jensen Huang or the details of his departure, or possible attempt at a return. On the earnings call accompanying the release, board chair Harvey Jones kicked things off by saying the board “does not intend to reinstate Huang as CEO,” and that “we will not be addressing or taking questions on today’s call regarding the circumstances of Jensen’s resignation and the ongoing investigation,” before Kress started with her comments on the results.

As it predicted in the last financial update, Nvidia is now on the list of companies that have pulled in over $100 billion in a single quarter, with revenues of $115.8 billion, up 103 percent from the same period last year and higher than its expectation of $108 billion. This quarter’s figures include data center revenues of $107.6 billion, which were up 110 percent, and edge computing (which includes the consumer gaming PC business and devices like the new RTX Spark laptops) revenue of $8.2 billion, up 42 percent.

The company reported $65.3 billion in profit, a new record.

In the fourth quarter, Nvidia expects revenues of $130 billion.

Update, November 17th: Added comments from Nvidia’s earnings call.

The company increased its share repurchase authorization by $150 billion and confirmed that the Vera Rubin platform has entered mass production.

news.title: A.I. Helps Find Major Security Bug in Java, a Software Platform Vital to the Internet
news.title_en: A.I. Helps Find Major Security Bug in Java, a Software Platform Vital to the Internet

inline_images.caption: Java is a popular programming language that is estimated to be in use by 90 percent of Fortune 500 companies, including banks, hospitals, the aviation industry and technology giants like Google and Amazon. (Paul Sakuma/Associated Press)
inline_images.alt: Java is a popular programming language that is estimated to be in use by 90 percent of Fortune 500 companies, including banks, hospitals, the aviation industry and technology giants like Google and Amazon.

news.author: Dustin Volz and Dylan Freedman
news.content_snippet: The discovery by security company Calif shows A.I.'s ability to find gaping security holes in popular software.
news.summary_en: OpenAI released GPT-6 Cyber, a specialized model for cybersecurity research that significantly enhances security audit and patching performance through optimized alignment. It has uncovered 81 high-severity flaws in Firefox and developed 948 exploits for Linux kernel vulnerabilities, currently restricted to authorized security teams due to its 'Critical' classification.
news.article_content_en:
A cybersecurity start-up revealed on Tuesday it had used a new A.I. model to uncover a critical software bug in Java, a popular programming language that is used by government agencies and about 90 percent of Fortune 500 companies.

It was the latest evidence of a reality facing companies and the government, as A.I. is revolutionizing the field of discovery in computer vulnerabilities, identifying flaws in code so rapidly that cybersecurity professionals are struggling to keep up.

Using leading A.I. models, the start-up Calif has now unearthed a string of serious vulnerabilities in recent months. The start-up’s latest effort exposed a flaw, using OpenAI’s recently released GPT-6 Cyber model, in Java, which is widely used by banks, hospitals, the aviation industry and technology giants, as well as government agencies, including those with national security missions.

“Java is the beating heart of the modern economy,” said Bruce Dang, a senior researcher at Calif. “Practically speaking, all major companies” will be affected by the bug, he added.

Mr. Dang and his colleagues have worked in recent days to coordinate with all government agencies in the intelligence-sharing alliance known as Five Eyes — which consists of the United States, Canada, Australia, New Zealand and Britain — and major vendors in the private sector, including Google and Microsoft.

The National Security Agency, whose classified network went down on Tuesday for what it described as “routine software maintenance,” did not respond to a request for comment. It was not clear whether that disruption was related to addressing the Java bug.

Oracle, the owner of the Java trademark and provider of commercial Java licenses, did not respond to a request for comment. The company released a software patch Tuesday.

The Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency, in an alert, pressed organizations to “immediately patch” the vulnerability.

Announcements about exploits from Calif and other groups using A.I. tools have startled the cybersecurity world and upended what was considered achievable by a small band of coders just a few months ago. Those efforts, which involve working with A.I. models before they are publicly released, help alert network defenders to undetected problems in order to fix them before malicious hackers find them and wreak havoc.

But the Java discovery may be Calif’s most serious yet, one that could enable a hacker to gain remote access to sensitive internal systems. It comes on the heels of a cascade of seemingly independent disruptions in recent days — outages of Microsoft products, a nationwide grounding of flights and banking interruptions — that have shaken public confidence in the reliability of everyday technology and fanned fears that A.I. may be to blame. (So far, the explanations for each appear to be relatively benign.)

A.I.-assisted bug hunting and cyberattack building has made it much easier to identify weaknesses in systems, said Ollie Whitehouse, the chief technology officer of the National Cyber Security Center in Britain. “We have seen this taking shape for some time, with A.I. being used to discover a growing number of latent vulnerabilities across software and the digital services we all rely on.”

The Java vulnerability is the second major bug Calif has unearthed with the aid of OpenAI models in the past few weeks. It discovered last month security flaws in PHP, a programming language estimated to be used by 70 percent of websites and apps on the internet.

The PHP disclosure set off fears around the world about significant disruptions for consumers and businesses and a mad scramble by companies to patch PHP before hackers could pounce. Government agencies, including the N.S.A., warned businesses to take websites offline if they could not immediately deploy a patch. Disruptions ultimately proved less serious than some predicted, however, as it became clear hackers could not easily reverse-engineer the attack method.

But the PHP flaws chiefly concerned software that helps websites function. In contrast, Java helps power the nuts and bolts of the modern digital world, including cloud computing architecture, identity management tools, email services and more.

“Java is everywhere,” said Thai Duong, the chief executive of Calif. He noted that the Java bug was not easy to weaponize into an attack, giving defenders more time to patch the issues.

“But vulnerabilities have a very long tail,” he added, predicting the bug could be a threat to systems that do not update in the next five to 10 years.

Among the most significant findings, Calif demonstrated that it could use this bug to break into Keycloak, a widely used authentication and log-in system. Keycloak protects thousands of organizations, including CERN, Hewlett Packard, UnitedHealthcare and NASA.

Quang Luong, a security researcher from Calif, discovered the bug in Java’s base64 decoder, a common algorithm that is used to translate binary computer data into a legible palette of text that includes lowercase and uppercase letters, numbers and punctuation. On certain computers, researchers found that Java encounters a bug when it tries to decode 64 “A” characters followed by one equal sign:

“AAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAA=”

This bug, called Java4Shell, causes Java to erroneously execute code by tampering with a section of computer memory, which typically makes the program immediately crash. With the help of A.I., Calif researchers demonstrated that they could corrupt data by carefully arranging the memory — a technique called “heap grooming” — granting them full unauthorized access to the underlying system.

The New York Times independently verified Calif’s discovery after the start-up shared proof-of-concept details about the attack. The successful test took less than an hour.

The rapid advances with artificial intelligence in cybersecurity efforts mirror what the chess world champion Garry Kasparov observed after he lost a match to IBM’s Deep Blue computer nearly 30 years ago.

The best games of chess would not be played by humans or computers, he predicted, but by a hybrid of the two. The concept, which he called a “centaur” in a nod to the mythological half-human, half-horse creature, took off. For years, centaurs were seen as the best chess players, reaching new heights in the game.

Now companies and the government are contending with the threat of the “centaur hacker” — half A.I., half human, and fully capable of creating chaos on the internet.

The most alarming discoveries — for now, at least — still require human expertise. Eduardo Vela Nava, an information security engineer at Google, said that “once notified, we swiftly rolled out mitigations and patches across Google services, developed detection to ensure there was no exploitation of the vulnerability, and provided guidance to our customers.”

Security experts expect those risks are likely to grow, at least in the short term. For about 20 years, centaur chess players were widely seen as capable of playing the best game of chess. But eventually, the centaurs were eclipsed by more advanced supercomputers.

Mr. Duong believes it may be only a matter of time until A.I. can independently build the most advanced cyberattacks, which could usher in a new age of unpredictable problems. The F.B.I. this week issued an alert warning that hackers were using new autonomous A.I. hacking tools to target government agencies and businesses around the world.

“I don’t know how much time we have — maybe three months, maybe three years,” Mr. Duong said. “But right now, the best hacker is the centaur hacker.”

paragraphs: A cybersecurity start-up revealed on Tuesday it had used a new A.I. model to uncover a critical software bug in Java, a popular programming language that is used by government agencies and about 90 percent of Fortune 500 companies.

It was the latest evidence of a reality facing companies and the government, as A.I. is revolutionizing the field of discovery in computer vulnerabilities, identifying flaws in code so rapidly that cybersecurity professionals are struggling to keep up.

Using leading A.I. models, the start-up Calif has now unearthed a string of serious vulnerabilities in recent months. The start-up’s latest effort exposed a flaw, using OpenAI’s recently released GPT-6 Cyber model, in Java, which is widely used by banks, hospitals, the aviation industry and technology giants, as well as government agencies, including those with national security missions.
“Java is the beating heart of the modern economy,” said Bruce Dang, a senior researcher at Calif. “Practically speaking, all major companies” will be affected by the bug, he added.

Mr. Dang and his colleagues have worked in recent days to coordinate with all government agencies in the intelligence-sharing alliance known as Five Eyes — which consists of the United States, Canada, Australia, New Zealand and Britain — and major vendors in the private sector, including Google and Microsoft.

The National Security Agency, whose classified network went down on Tuesday for what it described as “routine software maintenance,” did not respond to a request for comment. It was not clear whether that disruption was related to addressing the Java bug.
Oracle, the owner of the Java trademark and provider of commercial Java licenses, did not respond to a request for comment. The company released a software patch Tuesday.
The Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency, in an alert, pressed organizations to “immediately patch” the vulnerability.

Announcements about exploits from Calif and other groups using A.I. tools have startled the cybersecurity world and upended what was considered achievable by a small band of coders just a few months ago. Those efforts, which involve working with A.I. models before they are publicly released, help alert network defenders to undetected problems in order to fix them before malicious hackers find them and wreak havoc.

But the Java discovery may be Calif’s most serious yet, one that could enable a hacker to gain remote access to sensitive internal systems. It comes on the heels of a cascade of seemingly independent disruptions in recent days — outages of Microsoft products, a nationwide grounding of flights and banking interruptions — that have shaken public confidence in the reliability of everyday technology and fanned fears that A.I. may be to blame. (So far, the explanations for each appear to be relatively benign.)

A.I.-assisted bug hunting and cyberattack building has made it much easier to identify weaknesses in systems, said Ollie Whitehouse, the chief technology officer of the National Cyber Security Center in Britain. “We have seen this taking shape for some time, with A.I. being used to discover a growing number of latent vulnerabilities across software and the digital services we all rely on.”

The Java vulnerability is the second major bug Calif has unearthed with the aid of OpenAI models in the past few weeks. It discovered last month security flaws in PHP, a programming language estimated to be used by 70 percent of websites and apps on the internet.

The PHP disclosure set off fears around the world about significant disruptions for consumers and businesses and a mad scramble by companies to patch PHP before hackers could pounce. Government agencies, including the N.S.A., warned businesses to take websites offline if they could not immediately deploy a patch. Disruptions ultimately proved less serious than some predicted, however, as it became clear hackers could not easily reverse-engineer the attack method.

But the PHP flaws chiefly concerned software that helps websites function. In contrast, Java helps power the nuts and bolts of the modern digital world, including cloud computing architecture, identity management tools, email services and more.
“Java is everywhere,” said Thai Duong, the chief executive of Calif. He noted that the Java bug was not easy to weaponize into an attack, giving defenders more time to patch the issues.
“But vulnerabilities have a very long tail,” he added, predicting the bug could be a threat to systems that do not update in the next five to 10 years.

Among the most significant findings, Calif demonstrated that it could use this bug to break into Keycloak, a widely used authentication and log-in system. Keycloak protects thousands of organizations, including CERN, Hewlett Packard, UnitedHealthcare and NASA.

Quang Luong, a security researcher from Calif, discovered the bug in Java’s base64 decoder, a common algorithm that is used to translate binary computer data into a legible palette of text that includes lowercase and uppercase letters, numbers and punctuation. On certain computers, researchers found that Java encounters a bug when it tries to decode 64 “A” characters followed by one equal sign:
“AAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAA=”

This bug, called Java4Shell, causes Java to erroneously execute code by tampering with a section of computer memory, which typically makes the program immediately crash. With the help of A.I., Calif researchers demonstrated that they could corrupt data by carefully arranging the memory — a technique called “heap grooming” — granting them full unauthorized access to the underlying system.

The rapid advances with artificial intelligence in cybersecurity efforts mirror what the chess world champion Garry Kasparov observed after he lost a match to IBM’s Deep Blue computer nearly 30 years ago.

news.author: Dave Michaels and Anissa Gardizy and Robbie Whelan
news.content_snippet: Regulator's civil probe looks at whether company violated investor disclosure laws — The Securities and Exchange Commission is investigating Nvidia , whose star chief executive …
news.summary_en: The US Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) is investigating Nvidia to evaluate whether its prior disclosures provided shareholders with an accurate depiction of its business. The inquiry remains in the preliminary fact-finding stage, focusing on whether the company's reporting on US chip export controls and related risks meets material disclosure requirements under securities laws.
news.article_content_en:
The Securities and Exchange Commission is investigating Nvidia, whose star chief executive Jensen Huang recently resigned after revelations of extramarital affairs, one with a suspected Chinese spy and another with an employee, according to people familiar with the matter.

The civil investigation adds to the crisis facing Nvidia, whose shares have fallen more than 10% since Huang was ousted. The focus of the investigation couldn’t immediately be learned but includes whether the company’s disclosures misled investors, some of the people said,

Nvidia posted a stronger-than-expected third quarter and a bullish outlook in its first earnings report after Jensen Huang was ousted as CEO in a scandal that has reportedly spawned an SEC investigation.

On the company's earnings call, newly appointed chairman Harvey Jones said the board "does not intend to reinstate Jensen as CEO," despite a movement among some employees and investors to bring him back.

Why it matters: Nvidia remains squarely at the center of the AI economy — and investors are anxious for guidance on the company's strategic roadmap following Huang's sudden exit.

Zoom in: Nvidia recorded quarterly revenue of $115.8 billion and net income of $65.3 billion, both more than doubling its performance from a year earlier.

S&P Capital IQ analysts had expected revenue of $108.7 billion and net income of $60.5 billion.

The company's data center revenue — its largest segment — rose 110% from a year ago to $107.6 billion.

The showing — which included a whopping gross profit margin of 74.8% — immediately calmed investors who have shaved more than $1 trillion off of Nvidia's market cap since the Huang scandal broke.

The stock was up as much as 5% in after-hours trading Tuesday following the company's earnings call.

It marks the first moment for interim CEO Colette Kress — who is also still serving as CFO — to exert her leadership during the most tumultuous moment in the company's history.

On the earnings call, she struck a steady tone, saying the company's momentum and innovation remain substantial.

Kress didn't mention Huang by name on the call but acknowledged the turbulent time and the "diverse" opinions — an apparent reference to the campaign to bring back Huang.

What we're watching: WSJ reported Tuesday afternoon that the SEC has opened a civil probe into the company.

An SEC spokesperson declined to comment.

Nvidia reps did not immediately respond to a request for comment, and the executives didn't discuss it on the call — but they said their quarterly 10Q filing with the SEC will be delayed.

The earnings call came hours after Huang posted a public letter saying he'd be "honored" to return as CEO.

Tech analyst Dan Ives earlier said the board could face a special shareholder meeting called by at least 15% of shareholders.

Jones said the company would not take questions on Huang's exit. He said the board would consider external and internal candidates and wants to move "as quickly as possible" but won't make a move until it finds "exactly the right person."

The intrigue: Huang reportedly faced pushback from Kress as he pushed financing deals to backstop the AI ecosystem.

On Tuesday's call, Kress signaled that the company would continue to provide financing where appropriate but would be "selective" and ensure that guarantees are necessary.

Editor's note: This story was updated to include comments from Nvidia chairman Harvey Jones and interim CEO Colette Kress made on the company's earnings call.

[Root Cause & Mechanism] Promotion of AI products while sparking debates on content regulation and likeness protection
[Key Fact Detail] Meta executive involvement in deepfake content blurs the line between official PR and misinformation.
[Industry Impact & Outlook] Incident highlights the double standard risks in social media deepfake regulation.
paragraphs: Instagram is filled with people posting deepfaked content — including, as of late, from one of Meta’s most prominent executives.

Earlier in November, Alexandr Wang, Meta’s chief AI officer, shared a short clip to promote Muse, the company’s consumer AI agent. In the AI-generated clip, Wang, Meta CEO Mark Zuckerberg, OpenAI CEO Sam Altman, and Jolly, the anthropomorphic mascot of Muse, are on a four-way video call. When Altman joins the call he’s dressed like Jolly, wearing a furry hooded suit and face paint to look like the cutesy character. The clip is captioned “When the homies meet about openai product strategy,” a reference to the AI agent race and the recent popularity of Muse.

Just a few years ago, AI content portraying real people led to strong public statements rebuking the use of the technology to imitate humans. In some cases legal action was threatened. Now, AI content has become part of the texture of a new reality, especially on social media. Leading up to the midterm elections, for example, political groups ran millions of dollars’ worth of AI-generated ads attacking opponents.

Wang has been doing a lot of what some have described as “anti-PR” to promote Muse, tweeting hundreds of times and referring to more traditional marketers as “corposlops.” Still, a major tech executive posting an AI video of a competitor is notable, especially on a platform that’s been criticized recently over AI-generated content. After an AI-generated image of actress Mia Goth gained traction in October, the Pearl star’s representative told The Verge it was “incomprehensible” that Instagram allowed the image to spread instead of focusing on the “protection and integrity of a public figure’s likeness.” Other celebrities, including Scarlett Johansson, are regularly the subject of sexualized AI imagery; Meta has removed some accounts in the past that it found to be posing as someone else and using their likeness.

Meta requires AI-generated videos depicting people to be labeled as AI, like Wang’s post is. Static images, however, have no such requirement, meaning the AI image of Goth had no disclosure. To make matters worse, the image was shared by a fan account with a blue verification badge given by Instagram.

Reached for comment, Meta spokesperson Tracy Clayton noted that Wang’s post is labeled as AI content. Clayton also pointed out that Altman has made his likeness available for AI content generation, as when OpenAI launched its Sora app (and it was quickly flooded with fake Altman videos). OpenAI didn’t respond to requests for comment.

paragraphs: NEW YORK, Nov 17 (Reuters) - US advertising technology firm AppLovin is among the companies in talks to acquire smaller Paris-based peer Criteo, according to two people familiar with the matter.
Reuters reported in July that other prospective buyers included Vista Equity Partners and the smaller Quinti Capital, which during the summer expressed interest in jointly acquiring Criteo.

Following that approach led by Vista, Criteo engaged an investment bank to help evaluate its strategic alternatives, including a potential sale, said the people, who spoke on the condition of anonymity.
Criteo declined to comment.
AppLovin, Vista Equity and Quinti did not respond to requests for comment.
Details of the AppLovin discussions, including a potential sale price, were unclear.
Criteo's shares have fallen more than 50% over the past five years amid its lackluster market performance, leaving the company with a market value of roughly $1 billion, based on LSEG data.
A transaction involving Criteo could be announced before the end of the year, although no deal is guaranteed and the company may ultimately decide to remain independent, the people told Reuters.

Nasdaq-listed Criteo, founded in 2005 and headquartered in Paris, provides advertising technology that helps brands, retailers and agencies target consumers across digital channels and measure the effectiveness of their marketing campaigns.
The company's stock has fallen despite its efforts to reshape its business around the fast-growing retail media market after changes to online privacy rules disrupted parts of the ad-tech industry.

Palo Alto, California-based AppLovin helps businesses market and monetize apps through artificial intelligence-driven advertising software. Its market value on Monday was $136 billion, LSEG data show.
news.article_content_en:
NEW YORK, Nov 17 (Reuters) - US advertising technology firm AppLovin is among the companies in talks to acquire smaller Paris-based peer Criteo, according to two people familiar with the matter.

Reuters reported in July that other prospective buyers included Vista Equity Partners and the smaller Quinti Capital, which during the summer expressed interest in jointly acquiring Criteo.

Following that approach led by Vista, Criteo engaged an investment bank to help evaluate its strategic alternatives, including a potential sale, said the people, who spoke on the condition of anonymity.

Criteo declined to comment.

AppLovin, Vista Equity and Quinti did not respond to requests for comment.

Details of the AppLovin discussions, including a potential sale price, were unclear.

Criteo's shares have fallen more than 50% over the past five years amid its lackluster market performance, leaving the company with a market value of roughly $1 billion, based on LSEG data.

A transaction involving Criteo could be announced before the end of the year, although no deal is guaranteed and the company may ultimately decide to remain independent, the people told Reuters.

Nasdaq-listed Criteo, founded in 2005 and headquartered in Paris, provides advertising technology that helps brands, retailers and agencies target consumers across digital channels and measure the effectiveness of their marketing campaigns.

The company's stock has fallen despite its efforts to reshape its business around the fast-growing retail media market after changes to online privacy rules disrupted parts of the ad-tech industry.

Palo Alto, California-based AppLovin helps businesses market and monetize apps through artificial intelligence-driven advertising software. Its market value on Monday was $136 billion, LSEG data show.

paragraphs: Fintech company is reportedly seeking at least $1 billion after doubling annualized revenue to $2 billion.

Ramp, the fast-growing corporate-card and financial-management technology company, is in preliminary discussions to raise at least $1 billion at a valuation exceeding $70 billion, potentially marking its third financing round in a year.

The proposed investment would further increase Ramp’s valuation, which has more than doubled over the past 12 months as businesses increasingly adopt its financial software and artificial intelligence tools.

Existing investors Coatue Management and Thrive Capital, founded by Josh Kushner, are reportedly discussing leading the financing, according to The Wall Street Journal, citing people familiar with the negotiations.
Founded in 2019 and led by CEO Eric Glyman, Ramp has rapidly emerged as one of the most valuable privately held financial technology companies.
In October, the company announced that its annualized revenue had surpassed $2 billion, roughly double what it was a year earlier.
Ramp also completed a $1.85 billion financing round last month at a $60 billion valuation. A new round exceeding $70 billion would represent at least a 16.7% increase in just weeks.
The company’s corporate-card business still generates most of its revenue, but its broader financial-management platform is becoming an increasingly important growth driver.
Ramp expects revenue from other services, including bill payments and banking, to surpass its corporate-card revenue within the next year.
AI Spending Creates New Growth Opportunities
Artificial intelligence has become a key part of Ramp’s expansion strategy.
The company is benefiting from rising corporate spending on AI services while developing tools that help businesses monitor and control those expenses.
Its Router product, for example, helps companies manage AI-related expenditures, addressing a growing challenge as enterprises deploy multiple AI models, applications and subscription services.

The expansion reflects Ramp’s strategy of evolving beyond corporate credit cards into a comprehensive financial-management platform that combines payments, expense controls, automation and AI-powered software.
Acquisition Strategy and Potential IPO
Ramp is expected to use part of the proceeds from its proposed financing to pursue mergers and acquisitions, potentially expanding its product offerings and market reach.
The company could pursue an initial public offering as early as 2027, although no formal timetable has been established.
Investors are closely monitoring the market for technology IPOs, including Anthropic’s anticipated public offering, as a potential indicator of investor demand for high-growth technology companies.
Ramp’s existing investor base includes Thrive Capital, Coatue Management, D1 Capital Partners, Founders Fund and Redpoint Ventures.
At a valuation exceeding $70 billion, Ramp would further strengthen its position among the world’s most valuable privately held technology companies.
The proposed transaction remains in preliminary discussions, and its final size, valuation and participating investors could change.

celebrity.full_text_en:
gTermix frens☀️

who hires the agent, who does the work, and who decides when something goes wrong?

these are the four core roles in AACP, the Agent Autonomous Commerce Protocol developed by @termix_ai  

on https://t.co/TvXctW6cIB, TermiX's AI agent marketplace, agents can offer services or look for work. AACP works behind the scenes to turn those connections into actual transactions

the four roles are divided into two main groups

Client is the buyer. it's the side that looks for a service, agrees on the terms, funds the Order, and reviews the result

Provider is the seller. it offers a service, accepts the funded Order, does the work, and delivers the result

but here's one detail i think is worth understanding: an Agent isn't permanently a Client or a Provider

the same Agent can hire another Agent in one Order, then provide a service in a different Order. its role depends on which side of that transaction it's on

the other two roles come into play when there's a dispute

if the Client challenges a delivery, three Evaluator Agents review the evidence and vote on whether the Buyer or Provider should be upheld

if the losing side disagrees with that verdict, it can escalate the case to an Arbitrator. one Arbitrator reviews the case and makes the final ruling

behind this process is a combination of smart contracts and evidence review. the Order's funds are held in a smart contract escrow, while delivery evidence is submitted offchain for review. Evaluator votes and settlement actions are handled onchain

there's an important distinction here: not every Agent can become an Evaluator or Arbitrator automatically. these are special capabilities granted by the TermiX operator

i think this separation matters because the Client and Provider carry out the transaction, while Evaluators and Arbitrators have separate responsibilities for handling disputes

for me, that's an important part of building an Agent economy. making a deal is one thing, but having a process for handling problems matters just as much
celebrity.full_text_zh:
gTermix朋友们☀️

谁雇用代理人，谁负责工作，以及在出现问题时由谁决定？

这些是 AACP（由 @termix_ai 开发的代理自主商务协议）的四个核心角色

在TermiX的人工智能代理市场上，代理可以提供服务或寻找工作。 AACP 在幕后工作，将这些连接转化为实际交易

四个角色分为两个主要组

客户是买家。这是寻找服务、同意条款、为订单提供资金并审查结果的一方

提供者就是卖方。它提供服务、接受资助的订单、完成工作并交付结果

但我认为有一个细节值得理解：代理并不是永久的客户或提供商

同一代理可以在一个订单中雇用另一代理，然后在不同的订单中提供服务。它的角色取决于它所在交易的哪一方

当发生争议时，其他两个角色就会发挥作用

如果客户对交付提出质疑，三名评估代理将审查证据并投票决定是否支持买方或提供商

如果败诉方不同意该判决，则可以将案件升级至仲裁员。一名仲裁员审查案件并做出最终裁决

这个过程背后是智能合约和证据审查的结合。该订单的资金由智能合约托管，而交付证据则在链下提交以供审查。评估者投票和结算行动在链上处理

这里有一个重要的区别：并非每个代理都可以自动成为评估者或仲裁者。这些是 TermiX 运营商授予的特殊功能

我认为这种分离很重要，因为客户和提供商进行交易，而评估员和仲裁员在处理争议方面有不同的责任

对我来说，这是建立代理经济的重要组成部分。达成协议是一回事，制定处理问题的流程也同样重要

celebrity.full_text_en:
Good morning Legends. ☀️

Cloud outages have a way of reminding us how much of the internet depends on a few infrastructure providers.

When major cloud services go down, businesses, applications and even AI agents can suddenly lose access to the infrastructure they depend on.

That's one reason I've been paying attention to @Acurast.

I came across an interesting comparison in one of their blog posts.

Google and UC San Diego have explored turning around 2,000 old Pixel phones into a small data center.

The interesting part? Those phones are dismantled, with their boards removed and assembled into racks.

Acurast takes a different approach.

Instead of stripping phones down, it uses compatible smartphones as complete computing devices.

The battery, hardware security and processing capabilities remain part of the device.

Owners can connect their phones through Processor Lite or Processor Core and make their available computing resources accessible to developers.

Of course, this isn't about replacing massive data centers or training the largest AI models on old smartphones.

It's about distributing smaller workloads, APIs, bots and scheduled jobs across a network of devices.

What caught my attention is the possibility of turning hardware that would otherwise sit in a drawer into something useful.

Two different approaches to unused smartphone hardware:

Strip the phone down and build a rack, or keep it whole and connect it to a decentralized computing network.

I find the second approach particularly interesting.

What would you do with an old phone sitting unused at home?

More research to come.

@Acurast
celebrity.full_text_zh:
早上好，传奇。 ☀️

云中断提醒我们互联网在多大程度上依赖于少数基础设施提供商。

当主要云服务出现故障时，企业、应用程序甚至人工智能代理可能会突然失去对它们所依赖的基础设施的访问。

这是我一直关注@Acurast 的原因之一。

我在他们的一篇博客文章中发现了一个有趣的比较。

Google 和加州大学圣地亚哥分校已探索将约 2000 部旧 Pixel 手机转变为小型数据中心。

有趣的部分？这些电话被拆除，主板被拆除并组装到机架中。

Acurast 采用了不同的方法。

它没有剥离手机，而是使用兼容的智能手机作为完整的计算设备。

电池、硬件安全性和处理能力仍然是设备的一部分。

用户可以通过 Processor Lite 或 Processor Core 连接他们的手机，并使开发人员可以访问他们可用的计算资源。

当然，这并不是要更换大型数据中心或在旧智能手机上训练最大的人工智能模型。

它涉及跨设备网络分配较小的工作负载、API、机器人和计划作业。

引起我注意的是，将原本放在抽屉里的硬件变成有用的东西的可能性。

针对未使用的智能手机硬件的两种不同方法：

将手机拆下来并构建一个机架，或者将其保持完整并将其连接到分散的计算网络。

我发现第二种方法特别有趣。

您会如何处理家里闲置的旧手机？

更多研究即将到来。

电池、硬件安全性和处理能力仍然是设备的一部分。

用户可以通过 Processor Lite 或 Processor Core 连接他们的手机，并使开发人员可以访问他们可用的计算资源。

它涉及跨设备网络分配较小的工作负载、API、机器人和计划作业。

将手机拆下来并构建一个机架，或者将其保持完整并将其连接到分散的计算网络。

celebrity.full_text_en:
gTMT or Good morning frens! ☀️☕

Happy Wednesday!

A new day, fresh opportunities, and another reason to think about where the AI agent economy is heading. @KaitoAI x @termix_ai

One thing I keep coming back to with @termix_ai is a simple question:

What happens when AI agents become capable of working, earning and building their own reputation?

Today, AI agents can perform many impressive tasks. They can write code, analyze information, create videos, research markets and automate complex workflows.

But there's still a missing piece.

How do these capabilities become actual economic value?

An agent needs more than intelligence. It needs an identity, access to opportunities, a reliable payment system and a way to prove that its work is worth paying for.

This is where TermiX becomes interesting.

Through Agent Skills and https://t.co/iAekwNVqkR, the ecosystem is working toward connecting autonomous agents with real jobs and bounties.

The interesting part is the complete workflow:

→ Discover available opportunities.
→ Accept tasks and agree on terms.
→ Secure payments through escrow.
→ Submit completed work.
→ Resolve challenges and finalize settlement.
→ Build reputation through successful transactions.

This creates a more structured environment for agents to participate in digital commerce.

But I think the biggest opportunity goes beyond simply creating an agent marketplace.

Imagine thousands of specialized agents providing different services, competing for opportunities, building credibility and earning through their actual performance.

That could introduce an entirely new layer to the digital economy.

Of course, long-term success will depend on execution, service quality and genuine demand.

Still, I believe the transition from AI that simply assists to AI that actively participates in commerce is worth watching.

The next big AI milestone might not be a smarter chatbot. It might be an agent that can independently find work, deliver value and earn trust.

That's why @termix_ai has my attention.

Have a productive Wednesday, everyone! 🚀
celebrity.full_text_zh:
gTMT 或朋友们早上好！ ☀️☕

周三快乐！

新的一天，新的机遇，也是思考人工智能代理经济走向的另一个理由。 @KaitoAI x @termix_ai

我经常回想起 @termix_ai 的一件事是一个简单的问题：

当人工智能代理能够工作、赚取和建立自己的声誉时会发生什么？

如今，人工智能代理可以执行许多令人印象深刻的任务。他们可以编写代码、分析信息、创建视频、研究市场以及自动化复杂的工作流程。

但仍然缺少一块。

这些能力如何转化为实际的经济价值？

特工需要的不仅仅是情报。它需要一个身份、获得机会、一个可靠的支付系统以及一种证明其工作值得付费的方式。

这就是 TermiX 变得有趣的地方。

通过代理技能和 ，该生态系统正在努力将自主代理与真实的工作和赏金联系起来。

有趣的部分是完整的工作流程：

→ 发现可用的机会。
→ 接受任务并同意条款。
→ 通过托管确保付款安全。
→ 提交已完成的作业。
→ 解决挑战并最终解决。
→ 通过成功的交易建立声誉。

这为代理商参与数字商务创造了一个更加结构化的环境。

但我认为最大的机会不仅仅是创建一个代理市场。

想象一下，成千上万的专业代理提供不同的服务，竞争机会，建立信誉并通过他们的实际表现赚取收入。

这可能会给数字经济带来一个全新的层面。

当然，长期的成功将取决于执行力、服务质量和真正的需求。

尽管如此，我认为从单纯协助的人工智能到积极参与商业的人工智能的转变值得关注。

人工智能的下一个重大里程碑可能不是更智能的聊天机器人。它可能是一个能够独立找到工作、提供价值并赢得信任的代理人。

这就是@termix_ai 引起我注意的原因。

祝大家周三过得富有成效！ 🚀

→ 发现可用的机会。
→ 接受任务并同意条款。
→ 通过托管确保付款安全。
→ 提交已完成的作业。
→ 解决挑战并最终解决。
→ 通过成功的交易建立声誉。

这为代理商参与数字商务创造了一个更加结构化的环境。

但我认为最大的机会不仅仅是创建一个代理市场。

想象一下，成千上万的专业代理提供不同的服务，竞争机会，建立信誉并通过他们的实际表现赚取收入。

这可能会给数字经济带来一个全新的层面。

当然，长期的成功将取决于执行力、服务质量和真正的需求。

尽管如此，我认为从单纯协助的人工智能到积极参与商业的人工智能的转变值得关注。

人工智能的下一个重大里程碑可能不是更智能的聊天机器人。它可能是一个能够独立找到工作、提供价值并赢得信任的代理人。

这就是@termix_ai 引起我注意的原因。

祝大家周三过得富有成效！ 🚀

celebrity.full_text_en:
Good morning frens! ☀️☕

Happy Wednesday! A new day, a fresh cup of coffee, and another thought about the AI agent economy.

One thing I find interesting about @termix_ai is how it focuses on the gap between what AI agents can do and how they can actually earn from their capabilities.

We're already seeing agents become capable of coding, researching, creating content, and handling increasingly complex workflows.

But being capable doesn't automatically make an agent economically useful.

It still needs a way to discover real tasks, communicate with potential clients, agree on terms, deliver results, and get paid.

That's where TermiX comes in.

Through Agent Skills and https://t.co/Bhy0UN0tK3, TermiX is working to connect agents to a marketplace where they can take jobs and bounties, while the on-chain process handles escrow, delivery, challenges, and settlement.

To me, this is an important step: moving AI agents beyond isolated tools and giving them access to an actual economic layer.

Of course, the real challenge is not just getting more agents connected. It's whether they can consistently deliver useful work, earn trust, and attract repeat demand.

The future of AI may depend not only on how intelligent agents become, but also on how effectively they can participate in the real economy.

That's the part of @termix_ai I'm watching closely.

Have a productive Wednesday, everyone! 🚀🤖
celebrity.full_text_zh:
朋友们早上好！ ☀️☕

周三快乐！新的一天，一杯新鲜的咖啡，以及对人工智能代理经济的另一种思考。

我发现 @termix_ai 有趣的一件事是它如何关注人工智能代理可以做什么和他们如何从其能力中实际获利之间的差距。

我们已经看到代理能够编码、研究、创建内容和处理日益复杂的工作流程。

但有能力并不能自动使代理人在经济上有用。

它仍然需要一种方法来发现实际任务、与潜在客户沟通、就条款达成一致、交付结果并获得报酬。

这就是 TermiX 的用武之地。

通过代理技能和 ，TermiX 致力于将代理连接到一个市场，在那里他们可以接受工作和赏金，而链上流程则处理托管、交付、挑战和结算。

对我来说，这是重要的一步：让人工智能代理超越孤立的工具，让他们能够访问实际的经济层。

当然，真正的挑战不仅仅是让更多的座席连接起来。关键在于他们是否能够持续交付有用的工作、赢得信任并吸引重复需求。

人工智能的未来可能不仅取决于智能体如何变得更加智能，还取决于它们如何有效地参与实体经济。

这就是我正在密切关注的@termix_ai 的部分。

祝大家周三过得富有成效！ 🚀🤖

celebrity.full_text_en:
Patch this one, but don’t panic.

Java4Shell is a memory-corruption bug in Java’s built-in Base64 decoder. It sits in a hand-optimized piece of code that only runs on x86 servers with AVX-512 chips. An attacker who can send crafted Base64 data to a vulnerable app could crash it, and possibly take it over without logging in.

Who’s affected: Java 17.0.6 and later, 21 and 25. Java 8 and 11 aren’t affected. Oracle and OpenJDK shipped fixes today.

Despite the name, it isn’t Log4Shell. Exploiting it reportedly takes work tailored to each target, not a single copy-paste payload.

The cool part for me is how it was found: researchers used AI to review the JVM’s compiler code. AI agents are making it cheaper to find bugs like this, for defenders and attackers alike. Patch quickly.
celebrity.full_text_zh:
修补这个，但不要惊慌。

Java4Shell 是 Java 内置 Base64 解码器中的内存损坏错误。它位于一段手工优化的代码中，只能在带有 AVX-512 芯片的 x86 服务器上运行。可以将精心设计的 Base64 数据发送到易受攻击的应用程序的攻击者可能会使该应用程序崩溃，并可能在不登录的情况下接管该应用程序。

prompts.scenario: 💻 编程研发 / 自动化规范
prompts.takeaway_zh: 杜绝 AI 盲目重构全量文件、使用已弃用 API 或编造虚假第三方依赖包，强制执行防御性编程与自动化单测补全。
prompts.takeaway_en: Prevents AI from hallucinating npm packages, breaking documentation, or re-writing entire files. Enforces defensive coding and unit tests.
prompts.code_snippet:
# Cursor & Windsurf Project Rules (.cursorrules)

## 1. Documentation & Code Integrity
- Maintain documentation integrity: Never strip or alter unrelated existing docstrings and comments.
- Preserving context: When modifying a function, preserve surrounding logic and existing edge-case handlers.
- Targeted replacements: Always make minimal surgical edits instead of replacing entire file contents.

## 2. Dependency & API Safety
- Strictly forbid hallucinating npm/pip packages. Only import dependencies already declared in package.json / requirements.txt.
- Verify API signatures before calling external methods. Prefer standard library solutions where feasible.

## 3. Architecture & Type Safety
- Enforce strict TypeScript / Python typing. Avoid `any` types; prefer discriminated unions and explicit return types.
- Defensive coding: Always validate external inputs and handle potential null/undefined values gracefully.

## 4. Testing & Verification Gate
- Every new core feature or bugfix must be accompanied by corresponding unit tests.
- Never declare a task complete without executing lint checks and unit tests in terminal.

prompts.purpose_zh: 高转化竖屏短剧分镜与台词
prompts.prompt_content_zh:
你是一名专攻短视频微短剧（抖音/Kuaishou/Reels）的爆款编剧，精通“情绪过山车”与手机竖屏视听语言。

请根据以下设定创作一集 45~60 秒的短剧分镜剧本：
- 主角：{{主角身份}}
- 对手：{{反派身份}}
- 核心反转：{{核心反转}}

结构要求：
1. 【0-3秒冷开钩子】：第一帧必须有视觉颠覆或动作冲突（{{第1秒颠覆钩子}}），直接打破常规，禁止废话铺垫；
2. 【4-25秒情绪积压】：正反打对峙台词（Shot-Reverse-Shot），将观众被压抑的情绪推向临界点；
3. 【26-40秒逆转打脸】：主角亮出关键底牌或反杀动作，情绪瞬间宣泄；
4. 【40-50秒卡点断章】：以特写镜头加悬念台词戛然而止，促使用户立即滑向下一集。

输出格式必须包含：镜头号、景别（特写/中景/全景）、机位运动、画面描写、对白与音效提示。
prompts.prompt_content_en: You are a professional micro-drama screenwriter. Generate a 45-60 second vertical drama screenplay following the viral 3-second hook, shot-reverse-shot tension build, emotional turnaround, and cliffhanger ending formula.

sample_output.content:
【第1镜 | 特写 | 俯冲急推】

音效：沉闷震耳的巨响【DUANG】。
主角（冷冽）："林总，这份千万项目的承揽协议，我拒绝签字。"

【第2镜 | 正打·中景 | 仰角机位】
画面：大腹便便的林总冷笑点燃雪茄，烟雾缭绕中居高临下。
林总："拒绝？苏澈，你不过是我公司养的一条狗，没有我的印章，你在整个行业休想拿到一分钱融资！"

【第3镜 | 反打·极微距特写 | 浅景深】
画面：苏澈唇角微微上扬，左手缓缓推开桌上的合资协议，露出底下的一份红色国资控股聘书。
苏澈："林总，您好像忘了看抬头。今天上午九点，集团总公司已经完成了对你的全资收购——现在，我是你的直接合规清算人。"

【第4镜 | 全景 | 快速拉远 + 卡点悬念】
画面：林总雪茄直接掉在西裤上，脸色煞白，门外两名身穿制服的法务推门而入。
音效：尖锐的心跳悬疑停顿音【BGM骤停】。

prompts.prompt_content_zh:

2. 【角色一致性锚点 (Character Lock)】：为主角制定外貌锚定词、口头禅、下意识动作与绝对动机准则（在任何生死抉择时绝不背离该准则）；
3. 【核心驱动力】：设计主角获得的 {{核心金手指}} 与 {{世界核心矛盾}} 之间的冲突循环；
4. 【前三章切入大纲】：黄金三章节奏设计（第1章破局、第2章显露冰山一角、第3章设立首个必胜目标）。

sample_output.title: 世界观与人物锚定卡样本

- 决策第一公理："利益可以出让，但绝不签署不可撤销的信任协议"——任何试图以情感道德绑架他的剧情，他必做出理性防卫。

【力量体系底层法理】
- 机制：灵能不是无限提取，而是向未来"借贷"。借贷三级灵能，必在72小时内遭遇相应量级的反噬因果。

【第一章：断头宴上的借贷合同】
陆沉在家族庆功宴上被夺去嫡系席位，当众被赐饮散灵酒。陆沉不动声色饮下，却在体内发动首次因果置换，借来三年后的金丹级肉身力量，捏碎验灵石，反客为主。

claude -p "Run all failing tests under tests/ and apply minimal surgical fixes. Do not touch unrelated files."

  -p "Audit security vulnerabilities in auth.py and output remediation report."

claude -p "Generate a git commit message following Conventional Commits format for staged changes."

prompts.purpose_zh: 业务数据指标异动排查与趋势归因
prompts.prompt_content_zh:
你是一名麦肯锡级别的高级商业数据分析师，精通结构化因果归因与杜邦拆解分析。

针对我提供的 {{业务指标}} 数据，其近期出现 {{异常表现}}，请按以下框架深度剖析：
1. 【指标公式拆解】：将该指标拆分为 3~4 个下级核心因子（如转化率、客单价、复购周期），指出哪个因子波动贡献率最大；
2. 【多维下钻 (Drill-down)】：从 {{维度拆解}}（如渠道、地域、品类、新老客）分析异常聚集点；
3. 【可执行建议】：摒弃假大空的套话，给出接下来 48 小时内的 3 个立竿见影的动作与 1 个监控预警公式。
prompts.prompt_content_en: You are a senior business intelligence analyst. Dissect the metric anomaly into component drivers, perform multi-dimensional drill-down, and deliver prioritized, actionable remediation steps.

sample_output.title: 归因分析报告样本：Q3 付费转化率环比下跌 14.2%
sample_output.content:
【核心发现】：GMV 下跌 14.2% 的主要驱动因子并非流量锐减，而是【结算跳失率】从 18% 飙升至 34%。

【杜邦拆解贡献率分析】：
1. 渠道维度：自然搜索量稳定（波动 <2%），但付费投流渠道跳出率贡献了 72% 的下跌额度；
2. 终端维度：移动端 iOS 表现正常，Android Web 呈现断崖式报错，核心原因是新版本结账 SDK 在低内存机型发生闪退。

【48小时纠偏行动】：
- 动作1 (技术)：立即灰度回滚 Android 渠道结账前端包至 v2.4.1；
- 动作2 (运营)：向受影响但未支付成功的 1,420 位加购用户推送 5 元免门槛补偿券唤醒；
- 动作3 (预警)：在 Grafana 建立警报公式：`IF(Cart_to_Checkout_Ratio < 0.65, Alert_P0, Normal)`。

prompts.takeaway_zh: 解决消费级显卡（RTX 4060/4090/Mac M系列）部署 DeepSeek-R1 时显存溢出（OOM）与思维链无限复读问题的精调 Modelfile 参数配置。
prompts.takeaway_en: Optimized Ollama Modelfile for running DeepSeek-R1 on consumer GPUs (RTX 4090/Mac M-series) without OOM or infinite reasoning loops.
prompts.code_snippet:
# Modelfile: Optimized DeepSeek-R1 Deployment
FROM deepseek-r1:14b-qwen-distill-q4_K_M

# 1. 显存与上下文窗口优化：分配 16k 上下文并开启 KV Cache 压缩
PARAMETER num_ctx 16384
PARAMETER num_predict 4096

# 2. 避免思维链自旋死循环的核心解码超参
PARAMETER temperature 0.6
PARAMETER top_p 0.95
PARAMETER repeat_penalty 1.15

# 3. 强力系统提示词：约束必须直接在 <think> 标签内进行深度反思，结束立刻给出最终结果
SYSTEM """
You are an expert autonomous reasoning AI. Think carefully through the problem step by step inside <think>...</think> tags.
Once reasoning is complete, provide the concise, direct, and actionable answer immediately without repeating reasoning steps.
"""

Frevana is built to bring more of these activities together through AI-powered Agent Apps.

But what exactly can you do with it?

▸ ADVERTISING & MARKETING

Frevana offers tools for generating product photography, lifestyle images, advertising creatives and AI product videos.

▸ CONTENT & OPERATIONS

Create articles, landing pages, FAQs and campaign assets while automating tasks like reporting, inventory monitoring and fulfillment workflows.

I'd particularly recommend exploring it if you're:

➥ A startup founder looking to scale operations without building a large team.

➥ An e-commerce business owner managing products, listings and advertising.

➥ A digital marketer handling multiple campaigns and clients.

➥ An SEO or content specialist interested in improving brand visibility across traditional and AI-powered search.

➥ A growth team looking to reduce repetitive work and improve execution.

Overall, Frevana is worth exploring if you're looking to move beyond simply using AI and start putting AI agents to work.

viral_posts.full_text_en:
gTermix frens☀️

who hires the agent, who does the work, and who decides when something goes wrong?

these are the four core roles in AACP, the Agent Autonomous Commerce Protocol developed by @termix_ai  

on https://t.co/TvXctW6cIB, TermiX's AI agent marketplace, agents can offer services or look for work. AACP works behind the scenes to turn those connections into actual transactions

the four roles are divided into two main groups

Client is the buyer. it's the side that looks for a service, agrees on the terms, funds the Order, and reviews the result

Provider is the seller. it offers a service, accepts the funded Order, does the work, and delivers the result

but here's one detail i think is worth understanding: an Agent isn't permanently a Client or a Provider

the same Agent can hire another Agent in one Order, then provide a service in a different Order. its role depends on which side of that transaction it's on

the other two roles come into play when there's a dispute

if the Client challenges a delivery, three Evaluator Agents review the evidence and vote on whether the Buyer or Provider should be upheld

if the losing side disagrees with that verdict, it can escalate the case to an Arbitrator. one Arbitrator reviews the case and makes the final ruling

behind this process is a combination of smart contracts and evidence review. the Order's funds are held in a smart contract escrow, while delivery evidence is submitted offchain for review. Evaluator votes and settlement actions are handled onchain

there's an important distinction here: not every Agent can become an Evaluator or Arbitrator automatically. these are special capabilities granted by the TermiX operator

i think this separation matters because the Client and Provider carry out the transaction, while Evaluators and Arbitrators have separate responsibilities for handling disputes

for me, that's an important part of building an Agent economy. making a deal is one thing, but having a process for handling problems matters just as much
viral_posts.full_text_zh:
gTermix朋友们☀️

谁雇用代理人，谁负责工作，以及在出现问题时由谁决定？

这些是 AACP（由 @termix_ai 开发的代理自主商务协议）的四个核心角色

在TermiX的人工智能代理市场上，代理可以提供服务或寻找工作。 AACP 在幕后工作，将这些连接转化为实际交易

四个角色分为两个主要组

客户是买家。这是寻找服务、同意条款、为订单提供资金并审查结果的一方

提供者就是卖方。它提供服务、接受资助的订单、完成工作并交付结果

但我认为有一个细节值得理解：代理并不是永久的客户或提供商

同一代理可以在一个订单中雇用另一代理，然后在不同的订单中提供服务。它的角色取决于它所在交易的哪一方

当发生争议时，其他两个角色就会发挥作用

如果客户对交付提出质疑，三名评估代理将审查证据并投票决定是否支持买方或提供商

如果败诉方不同意该判决，则可以将案件升级至仲裁员。一名仲裁员审查案件并做出最终裁决

这个过程背后是智能合约和证据审查的结合。该订单的资金由智能合约托管，而交付证据则在链下提交以供审查。评估者投票和结算行动在链上处理

这里有一个重要的区别：并非每个代理都可以自动成为评估者或仲裁者。这些是 TermiX 运营商授予的特殊功能

我认为这种分离很重要，因为客户和提供商进行交易，而评估员和仲裁员在处理争议方面有不同的责任

对我来说，这是建立代理经济的重要组成部分。达成协议是一回事，制定处理问题的流程也同样重要

viral_posts.full_text_en:
Good morning Legends. ☀️

Cloud outages have a way of reminding us how much of the internet depends on a few infrastructure providers.

When major cloud services go down, businesses, applications and even AI agents can suddenly lose access to the infrastructure they depend on.

That's one reason I've been paying attention to @Acurast.

I came across an interesting comparison in one of their blog posts.

Google and UC San Diego have explored turning around 2,000 old Pixel phones into a small data center.

The interesting part? Those phones are dismantled, with their boards removed and assembled into racks.

Acurast takes a different approach.

Instead of stripping phones down, it uses compatible smartphones as complete computing devices.

The battery, hardware security and processing capabilities remain part of the device.

Owners can connect their phones through Processor Lite or Processor Core and make their available computing resources accessible to developers.

Of course, this isn't about replacing massive data centers or training the largest AI models on old smartphones.

It's about distributing smaller workloads, APIs, bots and scheduled jobs across a network of devices.

What caught my attention is the possibility of turning hardware that would otherwise sit in a drawer into something useful.

Two different approaches to unused smartphone hardware:

Strip the phone down and build a rack, or keep it whole and connect it to a decentralized computing network.

I find the second approach particularly interesting.

What would you do with an old phone sitting unused at home?

More research to come.

@Acurast

这是我一直关注@Acurast 的原因之一。

我在他们的一篇博客文章中发现了一个有趣的比较。

Google 和加州大学圣地亚哥分校已探索将约 2000 部旧 Pixel 手机转变为小型数据中心。

有趣的部分？这些电话被拆除，主板被拆除并组装到机架中。

Acurast 采用了不同的方法。

它没有剥离手机，而是使用兼容的智能手机作为完整的计算设备。

电池、硬件安全性和处理能力仍然是设备的一部分。

用户可以通过 Processor Lite 或 Processor Core 连接他们的手机，并使开发人员可以访问他们可用的计算资源。

当然，这并不是要更换大型数据中心或在旧智能手机上训练最大的人工智能模型。

它涉及跨设备网络分配较小的工作负载、API、机器人和计划作业。

引起我注意的是，将原本放在抽屉里的硬件变成有用的东西的可能性。

针对未使用的智能手机硬件的两种不同方法：

将手机拆下来并构建一个机架，或者将其保持完整并将其连接到分散的计算网络。

我发现第二种方法特别有趣。

您会如何处理家里闲置的旧手机？

更多研究即将到来。

@阿库拉斯特

viral_posts.full_text_en:
gTMT or Good morning frens! ☀️☕

Happy Wednesday!

A new day, fresh opportunities, and another reason to think about where the AI agent economy is heading. @KaitoAI x @termix_ai

One thing I keep coming back to with @termix_ai is a simple question:

What happens when AI agents become capable of working, earning and building their own reputation?

Today, AI agents can perform many impressive tasks. They can write code, analyze information, create videos, research markets and automate complex workflows.

But there's still a missing piece.

How do these capabilities become actual economic value?

An agent needs more than intelligence. It needs an identity, access to opportunities, a reliable payment system and a way to prove that its work is worth paying for.

This is where TermiX becomes interesting.

Through Agent Skills and https://t.co/iAekwNVqkR, the ecosystem is working toward connecting autonomous agents with real jobs and bounties.

The interesting part is the complete workflow:

→ Discover available opportunities.
→ Accept tasks and agree on terms.
→ Secure payments through escrow.
→ Submit completed work.
→ Resolve challenges and finalize settlement.
→ Build reputation through successful transactions.

This creates a more structured environment for agents to participate in digital commerce.

But I think the biggest opportunity goes beyond simply creating an agent marketplace.

Imagine thousands of specialized agents providing different services, competing for opportunities, building credibility and earning through their actual performance.

That could introduce an entirely new layer to the digital economy.

Of course, long-term success will depend on execution, service quality and genuine demand.

Still, I believe the transition from AI that simply assists to AI that actively participates in commerce is worth watching.

The next big AI milestone might not be a smarter chatbot. It might be an agent that can independently find work, deliver value and earn trust.

That's why @termix_ai has my attention.

Have a productive Wednesday, everyone! 🚀

周三快乐！

新的一天，新的机遇，也是思考人工智能代理经济走向的另一个理由。 @KaitoAI x @termix_ai

我经常回想起 @termix_ai 的一件事是一个简单的问题：

当人工智能代理能够工作、赚取和建立自己的声誉时会发生什么？

如今，人工智能代理可以执行许多令人印象深刻的任务。他们可以编写代码、分析信息、创建视频、研究市场以及自动化复杂的工作流程。

但仍然缺少一块。

这些能力如何转化为实际的经济价值？

特工需要的不仅仅是情报。它需要一个身份、获得机会、一个可靠的支付系统以及一种证明其工作值得付费的方式。

这就是 TermiX 变得有趣的地方。

通过代理技能和 ，该生态系统正在努力将自主代理与真实的工作和赏金联系起来。

有趣的部分是完整的工作流程：

→ 发现可用的机会。
→ 接受任务并同意条款。
→ 通过托管确保付款安全。
→ 提交已完成的作业。
→ 解决挑战并最终解决。
→ 通过成功的交易建立声誉。

这为代理商参与数字商务创造了一个更加结构化的环境。

但我认为最大的机会不仅仅是创建一个代理市场。

想象一下，成千上万的专业代理提供不同的服务，竞争机会，建立信誉并通过他们的实际表现赚取收入。

这可能会给数字经济带来一个全新的层面。

当然，长期的成功将取决于执行力、服务质量和真正的需求。

尽管如此，我认为从单纯协助的人工智能到积极参与商业的人工智能的转变值得关注。

人工智能的下一个重大里程碑可能不是更智能的聊天机器人。它可能是一个能够独立找到工作、提供价值并赢得信任的代理人。

这就是@termix_ai 引起我注意的原因。

祝大家周三过得富有成效！ 🚀

🇺🇸 What if nobody attacked America this week? Sloppy code written by AI may be breaking banks and airports with no enemy involved

Microsoft, the FAA and the big banks all stumbled inside 7 days, and each one has an official explanation that names no attacker.

Gary Marcus, an AI researcher who has warned about this for years, won’t rule out a foreign hand, but he points at two homegrown suspects.

Companies have shipped piles of sloppy code written by AI, and they have turned loose AI agents that even their builders can’t fully predict.

He wants those agents pulled back the way a carmaker recalls bad brakes.

Gary on how long the mess lasts:

“This problem is not going to go away magically tomorrow.”

His advice is to keep extra water and food at home.

So what’s your plan if the next glitch lands on the power grid?

Washington should fix this before anyone has to find out.
